mathematical_checks: Section-map resolution is isomorphic off the base ideal; divided coefficients generate the unit ideal.
Critical image dimension is strictly below the resolved projective image; Chow gives a homogeneous polynomial filter.
Positive maximum remains outside the base ideal and critical values; dd-c normalization matches the existing book curvature.
Kernel containment for two semipositive Hermitian forms gives the rank inequality.
Section ratios are merged into one positive degree; projective image dimension controls algebraic independence.
Book all-compact period count gives all-degree scalar upper growth; ungraded weighted spaces use inclusion only.
Fixed line twist uses dimension induction over fixed smooth divisor components, including repeated components and disconnectedness.
Projectivization uses the lines convention on E-star, so direct image O(1)=E; Serre duality uses the dual curvature of the same rank.
Analytic HRR applies on compact complex manifolds without a Kahler assumption; beta represents c1 and beta^(r+1)=0.
On surfaces the endpoint bounds and Euler characteristic control h1; no such separate intermediate bound is inferred in higher dimension.
Product sections descend along a connected compact factor; the binomial count is sharp for every0<=r<=n.
A fixed epsilon exponent loss cannot be upgraded to an arbitrary prescribed divergent factor; the latter is equivalent to O(p^r) for fixed data.
